name: Ernesto Guerra-Vallejos
headline: PhD Economist · Former Startup CTO · Staff Data Scientist
bio:
I’m a Staff Data Scientist at Direct Supply and an adjunct faculty member at the Milwaukee School of Engineering (MSOE University), where I teach graduate courses in statistics, data analytics and predictive analytics. An economist by training, I hold a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley’s Agricultural and Resource Economics Department, where I studied as a Fulbright Fellow.

For more than 15 years, I’ve worked at the intersection of economics, econometrics, statistics, and artificial intelligence — bringing quantitative rigor and causal inference to the machine learning models, deep learning models, prescriptive decision systems, and agentic AI I build, and taking them from research into production to deliver measurable outcomes at scale. Along the way, I co-founded Numeratti, a mathematical modeling LLC, in 2010; was appointed to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) consultancy roster as an Affiliated Economist for three years; held academic and research positions at universities in the U.S. and Chile; and worked at several AI startups, growing from AI Research Scientist to Director of Data Analytics and Chief Technology Officer.

My interest in business started in Tomé, Chile, selling potatoes and seafood at local markets during summers as a teenager, which led me to a bachelor’s degree in economics at the Universidad de Concepción in 2007. Resource economics runs in the family: one grandfather mined coal in Lota, the other saltpeter in Humberstone. Their stories gave me an early appreciation for both the economic value of natural resources and the human and environmental cost of extracting them — a legacy that drew me to Berkeley and to building AI for safer, more sustainable mining.
expertise: Agentic AI and the redesign of workflows around modern AI tools
Causal inference with machine learning and deep learning for business decision-making
Reinforcement learning, experimentation, and prescriptive decision systems
Edge AI and embedded systems — IIoT sensing, deep-learning condition monitoring
AI for mining and industrial operations
Climate resilience, water security, and commodity-price forecasting
Teaching and mentoring the next generation of data scientists
Intellectual property strategy for AI — protecting proprietary models, algorithms, and data assets
Commodity market fundamentals — storage, supply shocks, price spikes, and risk analysis.
